query:
Context: Our lab performs standards-based quantitative SEM-EDS (k-ratio protocol, NIST DTSA-II) at E0 = 5 keV on a Thermo Fisher Apreo FE-SEM with an EDAX Octane Plus SDD (takeoff angle 35 degrees). One standard is an UNCOATED bulk single-crystal MgO wafer (10 x 10 x 0.5 mm, epi-polished, mounted on a grounded aluminum stub, silver/carbon paint border planned at the edges). Our carbon evaporation coater is unavailable for two months. Scope: SEM / EPMA / electron-irradiation physics of BULK insulators and thin insulating films only; exclude TEM entirely.

Questions:

(1) DEPTH OF ELECTRON PENETRATION AND TRAPPED CHARGE IN CHARGING INSULATORS. What does the peer-reviewed literature say about how deep primary-beam electrons penetrate and where the injected charge actually comes to rest in an electron-irradiated bulk insulator? Cover: (a) the initial implantation depth versus beam energy (electron range scaling); (b) the depth DISTRIBUTION of trapped charge - the dynamic double layer picture (thin positive surface layer from secondary-electron escape over a deeper negative space-charge layer near the end of range), e.g. Melchinger & Hofmann 1995 J. Appl. Phys. 78:6224 'Dynamic double layer model'; Cazaux's analyses of internal fields and charge distributions (e.g. J. Appl. Phys. 59:1418, 1986); self-consistent charge-transport simulations such as the flight-drift model (Touzin, Goeuriot, Guerret-Piecourt, Juve, Treheux, Fitting, J. Appl. Phys. 99:114110, 2006) and Fitting's related work; (c) the SELF-REGULATION of landing energy: as negative surface potential builds, the landing energy falls toward the second total-yield crossover E2 so the penetration depth shrinks toward the range at E2 - published statements and measurements of this steady state; (d) experimental methods that measured trapped-charge depth or surface potential (electron-mirror method, Kelvin probe, x-ray/spectral methods, Duane-Hunt endpoint shifts) with quantitative example numbers.

(2) GROUNDING FROM BELOW: CONDUCTIVE LAYER UNDER A THIN INSULATOR INSTEAD OF A TOP COAT. Is there published work on analyzing or imaging uncoated insulators by placing the conductor UNDERNEATH - i.e., thin insulating films or sections on grounded conductive substrates charging far less than bulk insulators? Cover the physics quantitatively: capacitive scaling of surface potential with dielectric thickness over a ground plane (V proportional to thickness for a given trapped areal charge); electron-beam-induced (radiation-induced) conductivity within the irradiated volume allowing deposited charge to leak to a substrate that lies within or near the interaction volume; the condition that the beam range reach or approach the conductive layer; evidence from electron-beam lithography (insulating resist films ~0.1-1 um on grounded silicon wafers) and from SEM/EPMA practice (e.g., thermal SiO2 films on Si imaged/analyzed uncoated; thin sections on conductive substrates). Also: any work on deliberately BURIED conductive layers (implanted or deposited interlayers) for charge mitigation in SEM samples, and the known failure modes (fluorescence of the buried layer by X-rays generated above it; changed backscattering when the substrate is inside the interaction volume; thin-film versus bulk matrix-correction differences).

(3) MgO SPECIFICALLY AT LOW BEAM ENERGY. MgO has one of the highest secondary-electron yields of any material (used for exactly that property in plasma display panels). What are the measured secondary-electron yield curves (delta_max, E_max) and total-yield crossover energies E1 and E2 for MgO (single crystal, thin film, and degraded/contaminated surfaces), e.g. Whetten & Laponsky's classic measurements and later compilations (Joy's database of electron-solid interactions; Cazaux's reviews)? At E0 = 5 keV, does bulk single-crystal MgO sit ABOVE unity total yield (net positive, self-limiting few-volt positive charging - benign for EDS) or below it (negative charging by kilovolts)? How strongly do surface contamination, hydroxylation, and electron-beam conditioning shift delta and E2 for MgO? Any direct measurements of MgO surface potential or charging behavior under keV electron beams (including in SEM), and any published SEM-EDS or EPMA analyses of uncoated MgO?

(4) THE DUANE-HUNT ENDPOINT AS A CHARGING GAUGE. Published validation of using the bremsstrahlung continuum endpoint (Duane-Hunt limit) in an EDS spectrum as an in-situ readout of the true landing energy on charging specimens - e.g. Newbury's recommendations, Galvan Josa, Castellano & Bertolino 2013 Rad. Phys. Chem. 88:32 (quantification of uncoated non-conductors using the Duane-Hunt limit), and standard textbook treatment (Goldstein et al. 4th ed.). What magnitude of charging does it detect reliably, what are its limitations (statistics at the endpoint, pulse pile-up faking counts above the endpoint, time-varying potentials), and is 'acquire a spectrum, check the endpoint equals the set beam energy, plus stable count rate across replicates' an accepted accept/reject protocol for data from a possibly-charging specimen?

For every claim cite specific peer-reviewed papers, NIST publications, or authoritative textbook chapters with DOIs where they exist, give quantitative numbers wherever the literature provides them, and note honestly where the literature is silent or where values conflict.
